why: the read-vs-use distinction IS the eighth door; if the use shim answers .read, every spend path re-opens for a removed creator
isAdmin false is deliberate here; flipping it makes every background spend privileged
canWrite must be manage, not use; conflating them hands editing to viewers
old:
g := h.grantFor(ctx, userID, isAdmin, entryID)
	return g.read, g.manage
new:
g := h.grantFor(ctx, userID, isAdmin, entryID)
	return g.read, g.use

why: the load-bearing half: if an ACTIVE editor is silently denied, the whole matrix passes vacuously
note: MIS-SPECIFIED, not decay (verified 2026-07-31). This ablates an ASSERTION inside access_revocation_test.go and then runs that same test. Disabling an assertion can only make a test pass, never fail, so no run of TestRemovalEndsEverySpendPath can catch it. Verifying that a positive control still exists needs a structural meta-check, not an ablation.
